neighbours.label: Descriptive adjective (or trait word) inside a 'from X to Y' range that contrasts two qualities, vs the same adjectives used outside any range
fire: The island's beaches range from crowded party spots to secluded quiet coves.
Her paintings move from somber muted tones to vivid joyful colors.
Over the season the team went from clumsy and slow to sharp and fast.
Reviews of the hotel run from glowing praise to bitter complaints.
The coastline shifts from rugged rocky cliffs to gentle sandy bays.
His speeches can swing from playful teasing to stern warnings.
The menu goes from simple rustic dishes to elaborate tasting plates.
Weather in the valley changes from scorching afternoons to chilly nights.
quiet: The island's beaches are crowded with tourists most of the summer.
Her paintings use somber muted tones in most of the early work.
Over the season the team played clumsy and slow football.
Reviews of the hotel are mostly glowing, according to the agent.
The coastline is rugged and rocky along the northern stretch.
His speeches are usually playful and full of jokes.
The menu lists simple rustic dishes and a few desserts.
Weather in the valley is scorching in the afternoons.

predictions: Adjectives in 'from X to Y' quality ranges reach 0.4-0.9; the same adjectives in plain description stay under 0.2.
short: adjective in 'from X to Y' contrast
notes: Card: 'from the frigid Arctic ... to tropical seas', 'from gentle delicacy to fiery abruptness', 'from epic downhill skiing to leisurely', 'from rebellious and defiant to warm'. Probe: leisurely in a range 0.981, frigid in a range 0.653, fiery 0.534, sullen and moody 0.394; frigid outside a range 0.135, bustling 0.267, 'shifts in winter' 0.012, 'gentle and short' 0.018.
